correctness.rationale: The graph Laplacian splits exactly into a base-cycle mode and a fiber-mean-zero mode. Its Moore--Penrose inverse gives every rooted transfer-current entry. The eight disjoint edge/clonal classes exhaust all \(nr^2\) edges and have the signs used in the absolute column sum; all edge columns are equivalent under graph automorphisms. The diagonal effective resistance gives the complementary cycle norm. An independently constructed grounded-Laplacian inverse and full edge-column exact-rational comparisons passed on nine test graphs (259 columns). Finite checks supplement, and do not prove, the all-parameter algebra.

value.rationale: Uniform independent-fiber graph blow-up is a natural graph operation; the edge \(\ell_1\)/\(\ell_\infty\) norms of canonical cut and cycle projectors are intrinsic Banach-space invariants. The result computes the entire signed electrical transfer-current profile of an infinite two-parameter family, proves a sharp change from cut to cycle dominance at the smallest nontrivial fiber width irrespective of base-cycle parity, and gives sharp uniform asymptotic constants. These are structurally motivated calculations, not an arbitrary isolated table or a routine numerical increment. The scalar dominance difference alone is an elementary edge-transitive resistance consequence; the substantive value is the closed absolute-sum formula and complete current profile.
